title: Telemetry evidence capture manifest
description: Input to `python -m catalog_acceptance.telemetry_evidence_cli`. One document recording what was observed in Azure Monitor, from which the renderer produces the telemetry report and its four result files. Signal names, metric units and the report structure come from behavior-contract.json and must not be written here.

workspaceId.description: The Log Analytics workspace the queries were run against. Resolve it by name: two workspaces exist in this environment.

capturedAt.description: When the observations were taken, not when the manifest was written.

resourceAttributes.description: Must cover every name in behavior-contract.json telemetry.requiredResourceAttributes.

query.description: The KQL actually executed. Recorded so the evidence names its own source.

signals.description: Keyed by signal name. The set must match the contract exactly: no extras, no omissions. A signal you did not observe is a signal to go and measure, not one to invent.

recordCount.description: Zero is structurally valid so the renderer, not the schema, reports it -- the renderer names the signal and points at docs/TelemetryFaultInjection.md, which a schema violation cannot do.

observedAttributes.description: Must be a superset of the contract's frozen attribute list for this signal.

observations.description: Required for every traces and logs signal. The renderer will not default an empty list: an empty observations array is refused at render time rather than at the handoff gate.

measurements.description: Required for every metrics signal. catalog.import.records needs at least one measurement whose catalog.import.outcome is "rejected" with a positive, finite, integral value; see docs/TelemetryFaultInjection.md.
